title: Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.
- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.
- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.

Goals:
- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.
- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.
- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.

Prerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):
1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer’s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.
2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.
3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.
4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.
5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.
- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.
- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.
- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.
- Finance: confirms final billing state.

High-level decommission checklist (stepwise):
1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.
2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.
3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.
4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.
5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):
   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.
   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.
   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).
   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.
   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.
   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.
   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).
6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.
7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.
8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.
9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.
10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.

Commands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):
- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force
- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","mode":"secure"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
- Object store delete + verification (bash):
  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo "Bucket not found"
- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256

Evidence packaging requirements:
- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.
- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.
- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).

Verification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):
- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.
- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.
- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.
- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.
- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.
- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.
- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.
- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.
- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.
- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.

Rollback and exceptions:
- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.
- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.
- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.

Communication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):
- Initial acknowledgement to customer: "We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes."
- Final delivery message: "Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions."

Audit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):
- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).
- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).
- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).
- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.
- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).

Operational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:
- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.
- Accelerated SLA: 48–96 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).
- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.

Automation and tools:
- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/
- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.

Post-decommission monitoring (30 days):
- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.
- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.

Appendices:
A) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):
"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}."

B) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):
1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.

C) Emergency contacts:
- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)
- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)
- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule
